WORLD DOCUMENT · FIELD LOGIC Geometry defines the cone. Physics defines the pruning point.
Wall geometry links directly to field behavior. Passive pruning and Bottom / Air-Bag airflow remain active throughout the sequence, revealing one coupled hydrothermal interface.
KEY DISTINCTION · zp ≠ zh
UPPER PASSIVE BAND Passive pruning band Internal-cone bases form a continuous upper band where passive root pruning can occur.
LOWER OUTER BAND Outer airflow for Air-Bag Outer-cone apexes with openings form the lower airflow band feeding the Bottom / Air-Bag interface.
LOWER INNER BAND Inner airflow for Air-Bag Inner-cone apexes with openings regulate the corresponding airflow band from the internal side.
ROOT RESPONSE Threshold reading The field guides the root, separates outlet position from pruning front, and supports branching once the drying threshold is reached.
WORLD NOTE · FIELD PHYSICS Geometry Defines the Cone. Physics Defines the Pruning Point.
PAUSED

KEY DISTINCTION

zp ≠ zhin general

zh — outlet position

zp — actual pruning-front position

The outlet is not always the pruning point.

WHAT THE PHOTOS SUGGEST

  • Pruning may occur inside the outer cone before the apex reaches the opening.
  • Root bundles may accumulate around the bases of inner cones.

These observations motivate a model that separates geometric exit from physical pruning.

TWO PHYSICAL INTERFACES

OUTER CONE — air-facing interface: airflow, surface temperature, RH, vapor transfer and drying.

INNER CONE — compost-facing interface: temperature/RH gradients, moisture retention or possible condensation, and root guidance.

MECHANISM

Root enters a localized drying field → water loss / turgor reduction → apex growth stops → lateral branching can begin.

Pruning begins where local drying reaches the critical threshold: Φ(zp) ≥ Φcrit.

ENGINEERING TARGET

Do not design the opening alone. Tune the field so the pruning front appears where branching is most beneficial.

Primary variables: d, zh, H, θ, profile/ribs/texture, exposure/shading.

Two wall surfaces → Hydrothermal field → Pruning front → Root response
“We do not design the cone. We design the drying field around the cone.”
